Animation controls demo

All variants below use the browser's native video controls — no custom widgets. Same video (vp9_crf32.webm) in each. Right-click → Save Video As should work on all of them. Where native controls put the speed menu: Chrome/Edge in the ⋮ overflow menu, Firefox in the right-click context menu ("Play Speed"), Safari in the ⏩/AB controls.

All videos autoplay: autoplay muted playsinline — browsers only allow autoplay when muted (the animations are silent anyway, but the attribute is required by autoplay policy).

1. Browser default (zero JS)

Just <video controls autoplay muted playsinline loop>. Native behavior already fades controls out during playback and brings them back on hover; when paused they stay visible.

2. Hover-only controls

Native UI, but the controls attribute is only present while the pointer is over the video (touch: tap shows them). Video looks like a clean figure until you interact.

3. Trimmed native controls

controlslist="nofullscreen noremoteplayback" disablepictureinpicture. Caveat: this is a hint, not a rule — Chrome/Edge hide these buttons, Firefox ignores the attribute, and there is no cross-browser way to remove or restyle individual native controls (they live in a closed shadow DOM). Getting exact control over the buttons would mean building custom controls. Since hover-only hides the whole bar except during interaction, the pragmatic choice is to accept the native bar as-is.

4. Hover-only + keyboard frame-step

Variant 2 plus the one thing native controls lack: with the video focused (click it once), , and . step one frame back/forward (YouTube's convention), space toggles play.
